notes: Source: H3EK tags (F:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\H3EK\tags), read with ttk_common.flatten (private temp export); nothing in the kit was written.
Legendary = matg Difficulty [0] "imposs." column: enemy damage 1.60, enemy vitality 1.00, enemy shield 1.00, enemy recharge 0.30, rate of fire 1.00, burst separation 1.00.
Enemy pools = the character's "legendary body / shield vitality" (they replace the model maxima); the matg vitality / shield dials multiply on top.

Damage per hit = jpt damage upper bound (mean of the pair) x every matg damage-table [0] row for (jpt general_damage, specific_damage) x (material general armor, specific armor), materials resolved up the parent chain; missing row = 1. Player shields (and in Halo 3 the Chief / Elite armour) carry the specific armours energy_shield_thin_player / hard_metal_thin_player, but table [0] has rows for them only in no_damage, so they multiply by 1 here; every row looked up is listed per row under inputs.

Player times: continuous-time trigger simulation (ttk_h3family.sim_player): ramp lo->hi over acceleration time, bursts + fire recovery, heat with heat loss between shots and the overheated cool-down to the recovery threshold, reloads (magazine reload time; when it is 0 the reload is animation-driven: first-person reload_empty frames / 30). Constant-rate weapons are asserted equal to ttk_common.player_time.

Enemy shield recharge: character delay x matg "enemy recharge" (help: "enemy shield recharge scale") 0.30 -- ASSUMED to scale the delay (it falls with difficulty: 1.4 easy -> 0.3 legendary, so it cannot be a recharge speed). Flags use the scaled delay.

AI fire: the character's firing pattern for the weapon (from ai\generic; the minor characters define none of their own); the steady state of the legendary accuracy ramp is used (second firing pattern), the ramp start is in the flags. AI rate capped at the weapon's own rate. Paced = ttk_common.ai_times with the mean burst duration and separation.
Not modelled: headshots, melee, grenades, misses, AI weapon heat, damage falloff with range, the first-burst delay, damage-section (region) pools, Brute armour pieces.
AI default weapons come from a census of the squads in every levels\solo scenario (fire-team initial weapon, overridden per starting location); Halo 3 characters carry no default weapon of their own.
Halo 3 Elites fight on the player's side for most of the campaign; the Elite rows are measured as if hostile (Legendary enemy dials applied).
